arxiv-1710-05251.creator: Francesco Sorrentino 1 , Abu Bakar Siddique 1 ,and Louis M. Pecora 2 1) Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of New Mexico 2) Code 6343, Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, D.C. 20375
arxiv-1710-05251.description: Abstract Complex networks are the subject of fundamental interest from the scientific community at large. Several metrics have been introduced to characterize the structure of these networks, such as the degree distribution, degree correlation, path length, clustering coefficient, centrality measures etc. Another important feature is the presence of network symmetries.

arxiv-2102-09415.title: From Rényi Entropy Power to Information Scan of Quantum States
arxiv-2102-09415.creator: Petr Jizba *, Jacob Dunningham, Martin Prokš
arxiv-2102-09415.description: Abstract In the estimation theory context, we generalize the notion of Shannon’s entropy power to the Rényi-entropy setting. This not only allows to find new estimation inequalities, such as the Rényi-entropy based De Bruijn identity, isoperimetric inequality or Stam inequality, but it also provides a convenient technical framework for the derivation of a one-parameter family of Rényi-entropy-power-based quantum-mechanical uncertainty relations.

arxiv-2203-15085.title: Efficient and flexible causal mediation with time-varying mediators, treatments, and confounders
arxiv-2203-15085.creator: Iván Díaz, Nicholas Williams, Kara E. Rudolph
arxiv-2203-15085.description: Abstract Interventional effects have been proposed as a solution to the unidentifiability of natural (in)direct effects under mediator-outcome confounders affected by the exposure. Such confounders are an intrinsic characteristic of studies with time-varying exposures and mediators, yet the generalization of the interventional effect framework to the time-varying case has received little attention in the literature.

arxiv-2204-10364.title: Optimal Design of Best Response Dynamics in Resource Allocation Games
arxiv-2204-10364.creator: Rohit Konda, Rahul Chandan, David Grimsman, Jason R. Marden
arxiv-2204-10364.description: Abstract Designing distributed algorithms for multi-agent problems is vital for many emerging application domains, and game-theoretic approaches are emerging as a useful paradigm to design such algorithms. However, much of the emphasis of the game-theoretic approach is on the study of equilibrium behavior, whereas transient behavior is often less explored.

arxiv-2207-09857.title: Numerical modelling of imposed magnetohydrodynamic effects in hypersonic flows
arxiv-2207-09857.creator: H. A. Muir, N. Nikiforakis
arxiv-2207-09857.description: Abstract Weakly ionised plasmas, formed in high enthalpy hypersonic flows, can be actively manipulated via imposed magnetic fields - a concept termed magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flow control. Imposed MHD effects, within flows which exhibit multiple shock interactions, are consequential for emerging aerospace technologies: including the possibility of replacing mechanical control surfaces with magnetic actuation .

arxiv-2401-00519.title: Multiplexed entanglement swapping with atomic-ensemble-based quantum memories in the single excitation regime
arxiv-2401-00519.creator: Minjie Wang, Haole Jiao, Jiajin Lu, Wenxin Fan, Shujing Li, Hai Wang
arxiv-2401-00519.description: Abstract Entanglement swapping (ES) between memory repeater links is critical for establishing quantum networks via quantum repeaters. So far, ES with atomic-ensemble-based memories has not been achieved. Here, we experimentally demonstrated ES between two entangled pairs of spin-wave memories via Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller scheme.

arxiv-2503-12087.title: Temporally Consistent Mitral Annulus Measurements from Sparse Annotations in Echocardiographic Videos
arxiv-2503-12087.creator: Gino E. Jansen, Mark J. Schuuring, Berto J. Bouma, Ivana Išgum
arxiv-2503-12087.description: Abstract This work presents a novel approach to achieving temporally consistent mitral annulus landmark localization in echocardiography videos using sparse annotations. Our method introduces a self-supervised loss term that enforces temporal consistency between neighboring frames, which smooths the position of landmarks and enhances measurement accuracy over time.

arxiv-2504-10330.title: Can genomic analysis actually estimate past population size?
arxiv-2504-10330.creator: Janeesh K. Bansal, Richard A. Nichols
arxiv-2504-10330.description: Abstract 1 Keywords • Demographic inference • Sequentially Markovian Coalescent • Bottleneck • Population Structure • Range contraction and expansion 2 Abstract Genomic data can be used to reconstruct population size over thousands of generations, using a new class of algorithms (SMC methods).

arxiv-2507-15086.title: Topology and Algebra of Bonded Knots and Braids
arxiv-2507-15086.creator: Ioannis Diamantis, Louis H. Kauffman, Sofia Lambropoulou
arxiv-2507-15086.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ioannis Diamantis, Louis H. Kauffman, Sofia Lambropoulou. In this paper we present a detailed study of bonded knots and their related structures, integrating recent developments into a single framework. Bonded knots are classical knots endowed with embedded bonding arcs modeling physical or chemical bonds. We consider bonded knots in three categories (long, standard, and tight) according to the type of bonds, and in two categories, topological vertex and rigid vertex, according to the allowed isotopy moves, and we define invariants for each category.

pmc-10713869.title: Optimal timing for intubation in patients on non‐invasive ventilation: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-10713869.creator: Tatsuhiko Abe, Toshishige Takagi, Kazunari Takahashi, Kosuke Yagi, Ai Tsuge, Tomoko Fujii
pmc-10713869.description: Background and AimsThe timing of transition from non‐invasive ventilation (NIV) to invasive ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU) is uncertain due to a lack of clinical evidence. This study aimed to identify the optimal timing of intubation in patients with respiratory failure managed with NIVs.MethodsA single‐center observational study was conducted in Tokyo, Japan.

pmc-11684171.title: Bioinspired Metal–Ligand Networks with Enhanced Stability and Performance: Facile Preparation of Hydroxypyridinone (HOPO)-Functionalized Materials
pmc-11684171.creator: Declan
pmc-11684171.description: Bioinspired hydroxypyridinone (HOPO)functionalized materials are shown to display a remarkable capacity for stability and for chelating a wide array of metal ions. pmc-12567725.title: Isocaloric High-Intensity Interval and Circuit Training Increases Excess Post-Exercise Oxygen Consumption and Lipid Oxidation Compared to Moderate-Intensity Continuous Training
pmc-12567725.creator: Viviane Faleiro, Alexandre V Gurgel, Thiago T Guimarães, Tiago C Figueiredo, Felipe G Teixeira, Bruno Jotta, Estêvão R Monteiro, Alexandre G Meirelles, Carla C A Caldas, Maicon T de Almeida, Raquel C Castiglione, Silvio R Marques-Neto, Brendan O’Brien
pmc-12567725.description: Background: This study compared energy expenditure (EE), substrate metabolism, and excess post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC) during moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), high-intensity interval training (HIIT), and high-intensity circuit training (HICT) isocaloric sessions. Methods: Twelve trained male participants completed isocaloric exercise sessions equalized for EE and average power (AP) across the three modalities.

pmc-13214374.creator: Peggy Reuter, Jennifer Schroeder, Marc Sturm, Mathieu Quinodoz, Veronika Vaclavik, Miriam Bauwens, Marieke De Bruyne, Bart Leroy, Joseph van Aerschot, Katarina Stingl, Susanne Kohl
pmc-13214374.description: BackgroundMissense variants are frequently classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) according to the guidelines of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association of Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP). Consequently, disease relevance remains elusive, impeding molecular genetic diagnostics, patients` and family genetic counseling, and identification of patients eligible for clinical trials.

pmc-13372575.creator: Federica Gigli, Valentina Fabiola Sangiorgio, Valentina Tabanelli, Giuliana Gregato, Francesco Bertolini, Alessio Maria Edoardo Maraglino, Simona Sammassimo, Rocco Pastano, Enrico Derenzini, Corrado Tarella
pmc-13372575.description: BackgroundAllogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) represents the only potentially curative therapy in patients with high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, a considerable proportion of patients experience post-transplant relapse, a condition associated with relevant morbidity and an overall dismal prognosis.

pmc-13486289.title: Emotional resonance in the digital society: narrative mediation, platform hierarchy, and virtual consumption in cross-cultural sports communication
pmc-13486289.creator: Junmian Wang, Guojun Liao
pmc-13486289.description: This study examines digital emotional resonance in cross-cultural sports livestreaming through the analytical chain of host narrative–audience affective response–subsequent visible participation. Using the Chinese livestream of the Hakone Ekiden as an observational single-case study, we analyzed 97,878 publicly available interaction records collected across two race days.

pmc-13552805.title: Recommendations for optimizing the use of dysmorphic red blood cell counts in the clinical laboratory
pmc-13552805.creator: Oscar D. Pons-Belda, María José Ferri, Alejandro Almería-Lafuente, Cristina Izquierdo-Álvarez, Sergio Luis-Lima, Miriam Menacho-Román, Mario Román-Cabezas, Marta Sáenz-Valls, Elena Togores-Pérez, Patricia Fernández-Riejos
pmc-13552805.description: The assessment of dysmorphic red blood cells (RBCs) is of significant clinical interest in the evaluation of haematuria, particularly as a key tool for suggesting a possible glomerular origin. However, its actual utility depends on cautious, context-based interpretation supported by well-defined technical requirements.
